life_summary: Stephen Lyman Richards was born June 18, 1879, in Mendon, Utah Territory, to a family with deep roots in early Mormonism. The grandson of Willard Richards, a prominent apostle and pioneer, Stephen inherited a legacy of ecclesiastical leadership and intellectual achievement. He pursued rigorous legal training at the University of Utah and Columbia University Law School, earning his J.D. in 1904. Richards established a successful law practice in Salt Lake City and taught law at his alma mater, building a reputation as a skilled advocate and jurist. His combination of legal expertise and religious commitment made him an ideal bridge between the Church's temporal and spiritual operations.
church_summary: Richards was called as an apostle in 1917 at age 37 and served in the Quorum of the Twelve for over 40 years. He oversaw the Church's radio, publicity, and missionary literature efforts, modernizing Church communications during the mid-twentieth century. As First Counselor to President David O. McKay (1951–1959), he was instrumental in the post-war expansion of the Church and mentored younger leaders, including Gordon B. Hinckley. His teachings emphasized character development, legal and civic responsibility, and the relationship between Mormonism and American democracy. He demonstrated that ecclesiastical authority and secular expertise could be harmonized in service to the Church's mission.
